newsitem.title: USA: Jury in Reynolds trial to resume deliberations.
newsitem.headline: Jury in Reynolds trial to resume deliberations.

text.p: Jurors were scheduled to resume deliberations at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT Monday in a wrongful death lawsuit against the RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co to decide whether the company made a dangerous product and negligently caused the death of a smoker.
The panel, five women and one man, deliberated for nearly two hours late Friday after listening to more than five hours of closing arguments from the two sides.
Plaintiff Dana Raulerson alleged that Reynolds' negligence caused the death of her sister, Jean Connor, a heavy smoker who died of lung cancer in 1995 at age 49.

Connor began smoking as a teen-ager and developed a three- pack-a-day habit before she was diagnosed with lung cancer in 1993. She filed a product liability lawsuit against Reynolds a few months before her death. Raulerson took up the case as a wrongful death action when Connor died.
The trial, initially expected to last two or three weeks, enters its fifth week Monday.
